findings.evidence: The declaration proves `simplex₁ p = TauCeti.TopCat.simplex₁ ...`; the naming convention requires theorem names to describe their conclusions and uses a lower-camel namespace prefix when an otherwise ambiguous namespaced definition must be identified.
findings.fix: Rename it to a conclusion-descriptive name such as `simplex₁_eq_topCatSimplex₁`.
findings.issue: `GenLoop.simplex₁_eq` is too generic: it does not identify the right-hand-side `TopCat.simplex₁`, so users cannot distinguish or discover this comparison lemma.

findings.evidence: Line 122 concludes `(ιHomology₁ ...).hom 1 = HurewiczOne.H₁AddEquivHomology ... (HurewiczOne.loopClass ...)`; the adjacent line-136 theorem correctly follows the descriptive pattern `hurewicz_hom_one_eq_neg_loopClass`.
findings.fix: Rename it to include the equality target, for example `ιHomology₁_hom_one_eq_H₁AddEquivHomology_loopClass`.
findings.issue: `GenLoop.ιHomology₁_hom_one` names only the evaluated expression and omits that its value is `H₁AddEquivHomology` of `loopClass`.

summary: Two public comparison lemmas have names that do not describe their conclusions, contrary to Mathlib’s descriptive theorem-name convention.
